entries.clue: Beginnings of government restrictions that hurt whinger (6)

indicatorNotes.Beginnings of: the beginnings of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of government and restrictions
ouch is what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: A complaint that state restrictions have caused real pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'that hurt' reads as describing the restrictions, but it is the exclamation you make when hurt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name someone who is forever grumbling.

entries.clue: Good, on reflection, and chic somehow, getting balls on a plate! (7)

indicatorNotes.reflection: a reflection shows a thing back to front
indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow says the letters come out in some other order

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
ON seen back to front
the letters of CHIC rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone decides, after some thought, that a stylish plate of little balls is a good thing to serve.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'on reflection' look like 'after thinking it over'; in fact 'on' is the word being reflected.
annotation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small dumplings, often rolled into balls, served on a plate.

entries.clue: Dope ring: self-righteous Greek character flips (5)

indicatorNotes.flips: to flip something is to turn it over

blocks.note: a ring is O-shaped
pi is slang for pious, self-righteous
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A newspaper story about a drug ring in which a sanctimonious Greek suddenly turns.
annotation.walkthrough: Only MU turns over, becoming UM. PI for pious is an old schoolboy slang word crosswords still use.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: dope is slang for any narcotic drug, and the poppy extract is a classic one.

entries.clue: Smart to keep to a U-turn that's shambolic? (7)

indicatorNotes.to keep: to keep something is to hold it inside
indicatorNotes.U-turn: a U-turn sends you back the way you came

blocks.note: chic means smart, stylish
used as it stands
TO turned round

annotation.surface: A jibe at a government making a smart-looking U-turn that is really a mess.
annotation.walkthrough: CHIC holds A plus OT: CH-AOT-IC. 'Smart' looks like an adjective about the U-turn but is the outer word.
annotation.definitionFit: Shambolic and chaotic both mean disorganised and confused.

entries.clue: State axes Hair – "it's sinful!" (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a trespass is a sin, the thing that is sinful, not the adjective

indicatorNotes.axes: to axe something is to chop a piece off it

blocks.note: TRESS (a lock of hair) with its last letter chopped
a pass is a state of affairs, as in 'things have come to a pretty pass'

annotation.surface: A culture-war row: the state bans the musical Hair for being sinful.
annotation.walkthrough: Hair was a famously risqué 1960s musical, so the surface reads as censorship; here 'Hair' is just a tress, cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: Trespass is the old word for sin, as in 'forgive us our trespasses'.

entries.clue: Maybe Andy's shag alternative backfired (5)

indicatorNotes.backfired: something that backfires goes off backwards

blocks.note: to lay is slang for to have sex with
or introduces an alternative

annotation.surface: A dig at Prince Andrew, whose alternative sex life blew up in his face.
annotation.walkthrough: LAY OR read backwards gives ROYAL. Andy is Prince Andrew, and 'maybe' marks him as one example of a royal.
annotation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a member of the royal family, a royal.

entries.clue: Measure up cuffs i.e. fancy (7)

indicatorNotes.fancy: fancy means elaborate, the letters dressed up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A tailor's note: take the measurements for some fancy shirt cuffs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Measure up' looks like a tailor's instruction, but it is the definition: to be good enough.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to be good enough for what is needed.

entries.clue: Upset at Tories claiming Liam initially as "man of ideas" (9)

indicatorNotes.Upset: upset means knocked over, the letters thrown about
indicatorNotes.claiming: to claim something is to take it in
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, the first letter

blocks.note: AT TORIES rearranged
first letter of Liam, placed inside

annotation.surface: Tories are annoyed that someone called Liam is being hailed as a thinker.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters make ARISTOT-E around L. Scare quotes on 'man of ideas' hint at the sarcasm of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Aristotle, the Greek philosopher, is the archetypal man of ideas.

entries.clue: Anxiety when son replaces leader  –"beg your pardon" (5)

indicatorNotes.replaces leader: the new letter takes the place of the first one

blocks.note: worry means anxiety
S is the standard abbreviation for son, swapped in for W

annotation.surface: A parent's embarrassment when their son takes over and they must apologise.
annotation.walkthrough: WORRY loses its W to S. 'Beg your pardon' is an apology here, not a request to repeat.
annotation.definitionFit: Sorry is the one-word way of saying 'I beg your pardon'.

entries.clue: Maybe Russian billionaires' filthy rich goal is to get joy at last (9)

annotation.definitionNote: an oligarchy is the ruling group as a whole, so it stands for the billionaires collectively

indicatorNotes.filthy: filthy means messed up, the letters dirtied into a new order
indicatorNotes.at last: at last means at the end, the final letter

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
last letter of joy, added to the mix

annotation.surface: Filthy-rich Russian tycoons whose only goal in life is pleasure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Filthy rich' reads as one phrase, but 'filthy' is the instruction to rearrange 'rich goal'; the 's is part of the definition's surface only.
annotation.definitionFit: Russia's super-rich business elite are often called oligarchs, together an oligarchy.

entries.clue: Topical broadcast attacked by "patriotic" Trump supporters (7)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A news bulletin on a topical story about the January 2021 riot in Washington.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the news surface perfectly, which is why it hides as an instruction to scatter the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The US Capitol building was stormed by Trump supporters on 6 January 2021.

entries.clue: Father buries false report – a certainty for promotion? (5)

indicatorNotes.buries: what is buried is put inside something

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
a lie is a false report

annotation.surface: A priest suppressing a false story about a candidate tipped for promotion.
annotation.walkthrough: F-LIE-R. A high flier is someone marked out to rise fast; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
annotation.definitionFit: A (high) flier is a person expected to be promoted fast.

entries.clue: Space traveller's orgasm temperature (5)

blocks.note: come is slang for orgasm
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

annotation.surface: An astronaut's sex life, with a hot finish.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay rather than a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A comet travels through space on a long orbit round the sun.

entries.clue: Mate, maybe the Treasury lacks acceptable, handy means of prediction (9)

indicatorNotes.lacks: what is lacking has been taken out

blocks.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
the Treasury is a MINISTRY; take out IN (acceptable, fashionable)

annotation.surface: A friend jokes that the Treasury could do without its usual forecasting tools.
annotation.walkthrough: IN means acceptable or fashionable ('the in thing'). 'Handy' is the wit: palm reading is done with the hand.
annotation.definitionFit: Palmistry claims to predict the future by reading the lines of the hand.

entries.clue: Some finger pointing – which gives an idea of our economic state? (9)

annotation.definition2: which gives an idea of our economic state?

blocks.note: read literally: a finger that points something out

blocks.clueFragment: which gives an idea of our economic state?
blocks.note: a statistic such as inflation or unemployment that shows how the economy is doing

annotation.surface: Politicians blaming one another for the state of the economy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finger pointing' reads as blame, but it is a literal pointing finger, something that indicates.
annotation.definitionFit: An indicator points something out, and economic indicators show how the economy is doing.

entries.clue: Social function switches its political party – trickery! (9)

indicatorNotes.switches its political party: one party's letter is swapped for another's

blocks.note: a reception is a formal party
R (Republican) swapped for D (Democrat)

annotation.surface: A politician crossing the floor, denounced by former colleagues as a trick.
annotation.walkthrough: R and D are the US abbreviations for Republican and Democrat.
annotation.definitionFit: Deception and trickery both mean deceit.

entries.clue: Won't accept rubbish sex at first (7)

indicatorNotes.at first: at first means the first letter

blocks.note: refuse is rubbish
first letter of sex

annotation.surface: Someone turning down bad sex on the first date.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a verdict on the sex but it is the noun, refuse.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to turn something down is to decline to take it.

entries.clue: Dodgy seat, so something for the consumer (4)

indicatorNotes.Dodgy: dodgy means unsound, the letters not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A shopper warned about a wobbly chair.
annotation.walkthrough: The consumer here is someone who consumes food, not a shopper.
annotation.definitionFit: Eats is slang for food, something to be consumed.

entries.clue: Big supporter of CID employee getting raise? (1,3)

blocks.note: DC is a detective constable, a junior CID officer
up is the direction of a raise

annotation.surface: A detective hoping for a pay rise from a senior backer.
annotation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch. 'Big supporter' is a large bra cup, not a patron.
annotation.definitionFit: A D cup is a large bra size, a supporter for a big bust.

entries.clue: Cyclops's cut off when having erection – er, could be cellulose (7)

indicatorNotes.erection: in a down clue, erecting something stands it on its head, reading upwards

blocks.note: Cyclops is the setter, so Cyclops's is 'my'
to lop is to cut off
used as it stands

annotation.surface: The setter complaining of being interrupted at an intimate moment.
annotation.walkthrough: MY LOP stood upright in the down entry reads POLYM, then ER. The dash and 'er' mimic embarrassed hesitation.
annotation.definitionFit: Cellulose is a natural polymer, a long chain of repeating sugar units.

entries.clue: What the red-carded player did is untypical (4-5)

blocks.note: a player shown a red card has to go off the pitch, departing the playing area
an adjective from baseball slang for anything unorthodox

annotation.surface: A comment that a footballer's sending-off was out of character.
annotation.walkthrough: A red card sends a football player off the pitch for the rest of the match.
annotation.definitionFit: Left-field, from baseball, means unorthodox or unexpected.

entries.clue: Beastly complaint from former prominent socialist, Balls (7)

blocks.note: Michael Foot, Labour leader 1980-83
balls is slang for nonsense, rot

annotation.surface: A political grumble involving Michael Foot and Ed Balls, both Labour figures.
annotation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was a Labour minister, so 'Balls' looks like a name; here it means nonsense. 'Beastly' means of beasts, livestock.
annotation.definitionFit: Footrot is a hoof disease of sheep and cattle, a complaint of beasts.

entries.clue: Working men in Black Country (7)

indicatorNotes.Working: working means being processed, the letters reworked
indicatorNotes.in: in puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: dark means black
MEN rearranged, placed inside DARK

annotation.surface: Men working in the Black Country, the industrial West Midlands.
annotation.walkthrough: The Black Country is a region of England's West Midlands, so 'Black Country' reads as one place; they must be split.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Scandinavian kingdom is simply a country.

entries.clue: Old man, source of unlikely tips for Trump types (9)

indicatorNotes.source of: a source is where something starts, the first letter

blocks.note: pop is slang for father
first letter of unlikely
a ship that tips over to one side lists

annotation.surface: A father handing out improbable betting tips on Trump-style politicians.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips' reads as advice, but it is the verb for leaning, as a ship does.
annotation.definitionFit: Trump is a populist, a politician appealing to ordinary people against elites.

entries.clue: Son needs taking in hand – one of David's? (5)

indicatorNotes.taking in: to take in is to hold inside

blocks.note: the palm is the inside of the hand
S is the standard abbreviation for son

annotation.surface: A parent saying their boy needs to be taken in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: P-S-ALM. 'Taking in hand' reads as discipline; it splits into 'taking in' and 'hand'.
annotation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing many of the biblical Psalms.

entries.clue: Archer's release: 'Stuff 'em!' (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Stuff 'em!' is an imperative, matching 'Shaft!' used as a verb with 'em understood

blocks.note: what a bowman lets fly is an arrow
a dismissive curse: do them down, cheat them

annotation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, the disgraced novelist and politician, being released from prison defiant.
annotation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer was jailed for perjury in 2001, so 'Archer's release' suggests him; it is a bowman's arrow.
annotation.definitionFit: A shaft is an arrow, and to shaft someone is to cheat or screw them over.

entries.clue: Most favourable to ditch leader from an earlier period (5)

blocks.note: GOLDEN, as in a golden opportunity, without its G

annotation.surface: Political advice that ditching the leader would be best.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most favourable' is golden, as in a golden opportunity; the leader ditched is its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Olden means of former times, as in 'the olden days'.

entries.clue: Was sick brought up by this cook? (5)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, bringing up reads the word upwards

blocks.note: ailed means was sick

annotation.surface: A diner's sick joke about the food of a well-known cook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was sick brought up' reads as vomiting, but AILED is read upwards. Delia Smith is Britain's best-known TV cook.
annotation.definitionFit: Delia Smith is a famous British cookery writer and broadcaster.

entries.clue: Top of 1970s skirt removed by old male – an accepted fact (5)

indicatorNotes.Top of: the top of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.removed: a skirt removed is taken off, and here it is the skirt's top letter that comes off

O is the standard abbreviation for old
M is the standard abbreviation for male

annotation.surface: An old man taking the top off a 1970s skirt, stated as simple truth.
annotation.walkthrough: The maxi was the long skirt of the late 1960s and 1970s.

entries.clue: Boozer, at heart, represents this country (9)

indicatorNotes.at heart: the heart of a word is its middle
indicatorNotes.represents: to represent is to stand for, so the extracted letters are a nickname standing for the answer

blocks.note: the middle two letters of BOOZER

annotation.surface: A stereotype: the heavy drinker as national symbol.
annotation.walkthrough: The middle of BOOZER is OZ, which stands for Australia; 'represents' says the letters are a nickname, not the answer itself.
annotation.definitionFit: 'This country' points at the land that OZ stands for, and the boozer surface nods at a national stereotype.

entries.clue: Cyclops is backed in Tory rebellion (smaller faction) (8)

indicatorNotes.backed: backed means turned back to front

blocks.note: Cyclops, the setter, is I'M, read backwards
IN TORY rearranged

annotation.surface: The setter taking part in a revolt within the Conservative party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as the place the setter stands, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the lesser-numbered part of any group, as against the majority.

entries.clue: America needs time to change course and go on the offensive (6)

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for America
T is the standard abbreviation for time
a sailing boat tacks to change course

annotation.surface: US foreign policy shifting from caution to aggression.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Needs' simply joins A to the rest. Tacking is zigzagging a sailing boat into the wind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe starting an assault.
